title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Return of Originals When an Issued Document Is Corrected
content:
For several `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` types, a correction made after issue involves taking the issued originals back into the line's hands. This page states which types require this, what the returned originals become, and the time allowed for their return.

## Clauses

1. **Types requiring the originals back.** On a type marked "Yes" below, a correction to an issued document takes effect only in a state where no original of the set in force is outstanding: every original of that set is back with the line and the document's figure for originals outstanding reads zero. The record of originals outstanding on the document is the evidence, not the caller's assurance.
2. **What the returned originals become.** Originals handed back for a correction are entered in the documentation history as surrendered at the origin office.
3. **The corrected document.** After the correction, the document is issued afresh as the next set of originals, its set number being the previous set number plus one. No issuance fee is charged for that set.
4. **Lapse.** If the originals required for a correction are not all returned within the tier's return period, counted in calendar days from the correction request, the request lapses and is withdrawn.
5. On a type marked "No", issued corrections do not involve any return of originals, and the return period does not arise.

## Values by document type

| Document type | Originals must come back for a post-issue correction | Return period (calendar days from the request) |
|---|---|---|
| AHL Sea Waybill | No | 0 (not applicable) |
| AHL Electronic Bill of Lading | No | 0 (not applicable) |
| AHL Straight Bill of Lading | Yes | 14 |
| AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading | Yes | 14 |
| AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading | Yes | 14 |
| AHL Switch Bill of Lading | Yes | 10 |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A document of a type marked Yes shows one original outstanding. It is not in a state in which a correction can take effect. The same document showing zero originals outstanding is in such a state.
- On an `AHL Switch Bill of Lading`, a correction request registered on 2 September whose originals are all back on 6 September has not lapsed. If by 20 September nothing had come back, the ten-day return period would long have run out and the request would be withdrawn.
- On an `AHL Sea Waybill`, marked No above, a correction after issue involves no return of originals at all.

## Basis Q&A

**Is the corrected set a new document?** No. It is the same document, issued again under the next set number.
